Use the [AFM registers](https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/registers) to investigate the actual company. A familiar brand or foreign licence does not establish Dutch acceptance.

## Netherlands CFD rules for retail traders

The [AFM’s product-intervention information](https://www.afm.nl/en/sector/themas/over-het-toezicht-en-beleid-van-de-afm/toezicht-en-beleid/productinterventie) explains retail CFD restrictions. Leverage depends on the underlying; a broker may require more margin than the minimum.

| Underlying | Minimum retail margin | Maximum leverage |
|---|---|---|
| Major forex pairs | 3.33% | 30:1 |
| Minor forex pairs | 5% | 20:1 |
| Major stock indices | 5% | 20:1 |
| Gold | 5% | 20:1 |
| Other commodities | 10% | 10:1 |
| Shares | 20% | 5:1 |

These limits are not recommended position sizes. Use our [position size calculator](/tools/forex-position-size-calculator) to start with a cash-risk budget.

## What “best forex brokers in the Netherlands” should mean

- A clear company and appropriate permissions.
- Transparent spread, commission, swap and conversion charges.
- An understandable platform and useful support.
- Documented payment, complaint and client-money arrangements.

Compare scenarios with our [forex calculator](/tools/forex-calculator) and [profit calculator](/tools/forex-profit-calculator). Outputs depend on your inputs, not promised returns.

## AFM protections explained

Retail CFD requirements include asset-based leverage caps, account-level margin close-out at 50% of total initial margin, negative-balance protection and risk warnings. They do not prevent losses within the account. Professional classification changes protections; do not choose it simply for higher leverage.

## Investor compensation: what it covers

| Arrangement | Purpose | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Negative-balance protection | Limits retail CFD account liability | Does not prevent market losses |
| Client-money rules | Govern how client assets are handled | Not a return guarantee |
| Investor compensation | May cover eligible claims when a firm fails | Scheme, company and eligibility matter |

Check the home-state scheme, claim category and current limit. Do not assume every passported firm uses the same scheme.

## Payment methods in the Netherlands

Confirm SEPA, card or e-wallet availability directly. Check fees, minimums, currency conversion, processing hours and the return-to-source rules.

Once eligibility and terms are clear, consider a small deposit, request a withdrawal and confirm receipt. Successful receipt does not guarantee future withdrawals. Our [trading-platform guide](/insights/best-platforms-for-day-trading) helps assess usability before funding.

## Red flags to avoid

- Missing legal names or mismatched register details.
- Guaranteed profits or pressure to deposit.
- Payments to personal accounts.
- Unexplained withdrawal-release charges.

## FAQs

### Is forex trading legal in the Netherlands?

Access depends on the provider, product and customer classification. Check the exact company and relevant AFM/home-state permissions, including any incoming EEA service route. This page does not establish authorisation for every shortlisted brand.

### Which forex broker is best for beginners in the Netherlands?

Compare demo usability, education, complete fees and support after confirming eligibility. IG, Plus500 and AvaTrade are research starting points from this shortlist, not a tested ranking or guaranteed Dutch offer.

### Is negative-balance protection the same as investor compensation?

No. Negative-balance protection limits retail CFD liability. Investor compensation concerns eligible claims following a firm's failure under the applicable scheme; it does not insure ordinary trading losses.

## Final recommendation

Verify the company and Dutch service route before comparing platforms or clicking through an application. Practise with a demo, read the complete costs and use only money you can afford to lose. Leveraged forex and CFDs can cause rapid losses.
